The live configuration is the authority input for quorumSize()/checkLeaderLease() (raft.go:1036-1101), requestVote/requestPreVote admission (raft.go:1603-1813) and the election-start gate in runFollower (raft.go:158-260), so publishing an unpersisted configuration can change the node's own quorum requirement. The harness supplies a transient LogStore.StoreLogs failure at the real boundary (storage failure injection) on an otherwise healthy single-voter cluster that had just committed index 3. Observed (CA_EVENT config_publish_after_failed_durable_write): AddVoter returned the store error; the assigned log index 4 is absent from durable storage (getlog_at_assigned_idx_err=log not found, durable_last_index_after=3, raft_last_index=3); yet the node's published configuration now lists two voters (the real one plus phantom/phantom-addr). selections.rationale: A separate sourced observation found while auditing the configuration/authority path. Source: Raft.GetConfiguration builds the future as configurations{latest: r.getLatestConfiguration()} (api.go:897-903) and configurationsFuture.Index returns c.configurations.latestIndex (future.go:267-270), so the returned value carries the configuration but never its index; the main-thread path used by takeSnapshot (configurationsCh) returns the full configurations value including latestIndex (raft.go:667-965 leader and follower loop cases). Method: a bootstrapped single voter is elected leader, applies one command, then performs a committed configuration change with AddNonvoter, which keeps the single-voter quorum so it commits. The harness then reads the public future and, the same way takeSnapshot does, asks the main thread for the internal configurations. Observed (CA_EVENT public_configuration_index): add_nonvoter_error nil, add_nonvoter_index 4, public_config_index 0, internal_config_index 4, index_reported_as_zero true, indexes_disagree true, and public_servers equal internal_servers, so the public API returns the correct configuration value with a zero index while the node itself tracks configuration index 4. Boundaries: this is a conditional observation on fixed code in one in-process single-voter cluster; it does not by itself cause a safety or liveness failure, and its practical effect is that a caller who reads GetConfiguration().Index() to obtain the configuration index used as the prevIndex guard accepted by AddVoter/RemoveServer/DemoteVoter will instead pass 0, which means no constraint, and the Stats field latest_configuration_index is reported as zero for every node. This observ ation is recorded separately from the confirmed published-configuration violation (direct check 3b256fe6f42b4154b75d4d2ec02e27bf) and does not change it.

feedback.answered: No in-tree caller relies on GetConfiguration().Index() as the prevIndex guard, and the only in-tree consumer of that index value is Stats. The membership-change APIs take prevIndex as a caller-supplied parameter (api.go:946-1005) and the deprecated AddPeer/RemovePeer helpers hardcode prevIndex 0 (api.go:908-944), while nextConfiguration only compares prevIndex with the node's own current configuration index (configuration.go:229-230), so nothing in the tree derives prevIndex from GetConfiguration().Index(). Call sites of GetConfiguration are the package-level GetConfiguration helper (api.go:453), Stats (api.go:1183), the test cluster helper (testing.go:682) and tests (raft_test.go:172, raft_test.go:2690); of these only Stats reads the future Index, reporting it as latest_configuration_index, so a zero value there is wrong on every node but no membership-change safety property depends on it. The documentation does not create a pattern either: docs/README.md:61 describes GetConfiguration as returning the latest cluster configuration without mentioning an index, and membership.md:33 describes it as waiting for the latest config to commit, which does not match the implementation either.
